Advent International Looking for More Australia Healthcare Opportunities — Interview
By Stuart Condie

SYDNEY--Advent International is looking for further healthcare opportunities in Australia and New Zealand following its acquisition of a clinical-research network, the head of the U.S. private-equity firm's Australia office said.

Last month, Advent agreed to acquire a controlling stake in New Zealand Clinical Research from existing shareholders including Auckland-based Waterman Capital. Financial terms weren't disclosed but the transaction valued NZCR at about $715 million.

The acquisition continued Boston-based Advent's recent growth in Asia-Pacific. In January, Advent opened an office in Tokyo and five months later made its first direct investment in Japan with the acquisition of Japan Wellbeing, a provider of home care for the aged.
The acquisition of NZCR was the second by Advent's Australia office, which opened in Sydney in 2024.
Beau Dixon, managing director and head of Australia and New Zealand at Advent, said he approached Waterman after identifying NZCR as a target, and sealed the deal without competition.
"It remained proprietary, no process, confidential and very, very closely managed," Dixon said in an interview in August.

Dixon said Advent saw potential to double NZCR's annual revenue within three to five years of ownership through organic growth. At the same time, Advent is actively seeking further regional opportunities, he said.

"NZCR has its own opportunities for growth. We're not currently looking at acquisitions that are directly adjacent to that value chain," Dixon said. "We are looking at other areas in health where we feel that we have the requisite conviction based on prior experience."

Dixon said Advent's global reach, with assets under management totaling $94 billion, allowed it to build a pipeline of opportunities that it typically worked on for up to 18 months before closing a transaction.

For the NZCR deal, which Advent expects to close in the December quarter, Dixon said he was assisted by U.S.-based colleagues with deep healthcare expertise and experience including on earlier Advent deals involving pharma-research services provider Syneos Health and biotechnology manufacturer Simtra.
"There is no time limit on when we could sign the next deal and there's no specific pressure around that," he said. "The support is there for these high conviction opportunities."
